title: Chapter 70
content:
The tip of the knife tapped against the mahogany edge in a steady, rhythmic cadence.

Bound to a chair opposite sat a man with permed, disheveled hair, his face a swollen mass of crimson bruising beneath heavy duct tape.

Il-hyun ran his thumb along the flat of the steel before pressing the point firmly against the man's exposed windpipe. Dark veins bulged across the hostage's neck as muffled, frantic groans bled past the adhesive. At a single nod from his employer, Tae-soo reached forward and ripped the tape away.

In the next breath, the steel glided down and plunged straight into the man's left thigh.

A high, ragged shriek tore through the executive office. As Il-hyun pulled the blade free, dark blood erupted from the puncture. He leaned in, driving his bare thumb directly into the open wound, working it deeper with a pleasant, razor-thin smile.

The man screamed bloody murder, his bound frame thrashing against the chair legs.

Il-hyun blotted the crimson from his fingers with a clean linen cloth, holding eye contact with the broker.

"A little honesty from the start saves everyone a great deal of exhaustion, don't you agree, President Kim?"

The broker’s jaw rattled in pure, unadulterated agony. The man was notorious in the maritime underworld for arranging untraceable smuggling routes and high-grade forged credentials—a fixer who had facilitated Jakyeong and Ryun’s offshore extraction the year prior.

"I swear... I don't know anything," the man gasped through broken sobs. "Nothing at all..."

Il-hyun clicked his tongue in mild disappointment, extending an open hand toward Tae-soo.

A heavy pair of surgical steel extraction forceps was placed into his grip. Two enforcers stepped forward, locking the broker's shoulders to the frame. The man's pupils dilated in absolute horror as Il-hyun caught his jaw in a bone-crushing grip, forcing his mouth wide open.

Il-hyun slid the cold steel clamp inside, seizing the tip of the man's tongue, his expression settling into an arctic stillness.

"Since speaking seems so dreadfully inconvenient, perhaps we should relieve you of the burden altogether."

He brought the bloodstained blade toward the clamped tissue. The broker shook his head violently, grunting frantic, unintelligible syllables through his locked throat. Il-hyun leveled the edge directly before the man's widening eyes.

"Hush now. We won't stop at the tongue if you keep squirming. Though I suppose I could leave half... just so you can still taste your soup."

The blade pressed into the pink flesh.

The broker’s throat worked frantically, his muffled groans carrying the unmistakable cadence of surrender. Il-hyun released his grip on the jaw, staring down into the bloodshot, weeping eyes.

"Ready to converse like civilized gentlemen?"

The broker slumped forward in defeat, a heavy shudder running through his frame before he muttered in a defeated rasp:

"I don't know the exact coordinates..."

Il-hyun made a subtle motion to raise the clamp again, prompting the man to shriek in sheer panic:

"Jeonnam! They only asked for an inshore vessel down in Jeollanam-do! That is all I know, I swear to God! Why would I lie to you?!"

"Jeonnam?"

The region was an unexpected variable. Il-hyun’s eyes drifted toward Tae-soo, recalling his security chief's background—Tae-soo had spent part of his active service running black-ops maritime drills among the southern archipelagos. The province contained the densest cluster of uninhabited islands in the entire peninsula; hopping between forgotten rocks could keep a crew off the grid for months.

Catching the look, Tae-soo offered a subtle, affirmative nod.

"Tae-soo."

"Yes, President Kang."

"Scramble everything with a propeller or a hull."

"Understood, sir."

Il-hyun tossed the bloody knife to the floor, letting out a low, breathless laugh.

An abandoned rock off the southern coast? Out of all the places on earth... you ran to a deserted island?

Savor your little taste of paradise, darling.

Because I'm coming to collect you personally.
"Look at this bounty. An absolute feast."

Kneeling on the rocky shore, Wang Ryun skillfully dressed a feral black goat with his hunting knife. He had hiked up the island's central ridge at dawn, returning with fresh game in tow. Dropping Ryun into any corner of the globe usually resulted in immediate survival, but mastering a desolate rock within forty-eight hours was impressive even for him.

Tending the fire nearby, Jakyeong threaded chunks of meat onto shaved pine skewers, arranging them along the stones surrounding the embers. Though kept from direct flame, the fat soon began sizzling, sending the rich aroma of roasted meat into the salt air.

After days of dry rations and instant noodles, the smell had his mouth watering.

"Forget ten days," Ryun remarked, wiping his blade on his trousers. "We could easily hold out here for a month."

Jakyeong hummed in quiet agreement. Aside from the vicious swarms of coastal mosquitoes, the retreat was proving surprisingly tolerable.

A short distance down the beach, Wang Han stood balanced on a cluster of tidal rocks, wielding a fire-hardened wooden spear to hunt in the shallows.

With the goat needing time to slow-roast, Jakyeong waded out into the surf. The continental shelf dropped sharply, submerging him to his waist within a few paces. Taking a deep breath, he dove beneath the surface, scanning the seabed for abalone or edible shellfish.

The sandy floor was barren. He breached the surface with a spray of seawater, letting the gentle swell carry his weight as he floated on his back beneath the open sky.

Floating face-up in the water brought Kang Il-hyun’s silhouette back into focus—the memory of the man suspended in the illuminated pool just days ago.

Was he genuinely grieving that night?

Why am I still letting that bastard occupy my head out here?

Frustrated with himself, Jakyeong ducked beneath the surface repeatedly to wash the fog away, made a futile grab for a passing school of fish, and finally waded back onto the sand empty-handed.

Ryun was already seated by the fire, waving a bottle of clear vodka. "Wei! Hurry up, the skewers are ready."

Han returned from the rocks carrying a plastic basin containing two sizable octopuses. Jakyeong hoisted an old cast-iron pot over the coals, submerging the catch in seawater. The thrashing tentacles gradually subsided, releasing a savory, briny steam that blended with the roasting meat.

"I'm actually growing fond of this place," Ryun said with a grin. "Maybe I should set up my marital home right here."

"I'm sure your future bride would be absolutely thrilled to live in a garbage heap," Han deadpanned, passing around the roasted skewers.

Ryun poured generous measures of vodka into plastic cups. Taking a bite of the roasted goat, Jakyeong’s expression turned deeply conflicted.

"It feels like chewing through a steel radial tire..."

"What are you talking about? It gets more flavorful the longer you work it."

"Here, take mine then."

"I'm suddenly stuffed."

"We should have hunted seabirds instead."

"Not a bad idea," Ryun noted. "There's an old bolt-action rifle stashed inside the cabin. Rusted around the receiver, but a little gun oil will get it cycling."

Chewing the tender octopus and washing it down with cold vodka, the conversation drifted toward their early days in Macau, trading memories beneath the vast canopy of stars. As the sun dipped toward the maritime horizon, the entire sky bruised into brilliant layers of crimson, violet, and burning gold.

Ryun rose to his feet, stretching his arms toward the sunset. "Goddamn... that is one hell of a view."

Jakyeong and Han looked out across the water in silent agreement.

Just then, a distant silhouette appeared against the clouds—a twin-engine chopper cutting across the skyline. Ryun waved his arms above his head with a lit cigarette between his teeth, hollering into the wind:

"Help! Stranded souls over here! Save us!"

A little buzzed from the liquor, Jakyeong leaned back against the driftwood, chuckling at the theatrical performance.

Han frowned, gesturing for Ryun to drop his hands. "Cut it out. It's actually turning around."

Ryun waved his hands frantically to wave the aircraft off. "Never mind! False alarm! We're on vacation, keep flying!"

The helicopter showed zero intention of departing. Descending rapidly, the heavy downwash from the rotors began whipping across the cove, churning the surf into white foam.

Jakyeong’s posture stiffened. The airframe carried neither military roundels nor coast guard insignia.

The aircraft banked sharply, hovering barely fifty feet above the shoreline.

The heavy side door slid back.

The bite of octopus slipped from Jakyeong’s lips, tumbling onto the sand.

"What the fuck..." Ryun breathed, stumbling back a step as if staring at a phantom.

Kneeling in the open doorway of the cabin with a heavy precision sniper rifle rested against his shoulder was Kang Il-hyun.

Rotor wash tore through the campsite, scattering burning embers and gear across the gravel. Before anyone could process the visual, a sustained volley of high-caliber rounds chewed through the sand around their boots.

"Run!" Ryun roared, wheeling toward the treeline.

The three bolted into the dense brush as heavy rounds shattered the surrounding pines, tearing bark and branches into airborne splinters.

Jakyeong’s mind went blank with pure disbelief. It's only been three days. How did that demon track us to this forgotten rock?

They burst through the cabin door, gasping for air as the deafening roar of the rotors circled directly overhead. Jakyeong tore through the storage nook, hauling out the vintage hunting rifle. The action was heavily pitted with surface rust, but racking the bolt confirmed the firing pin was functional.

As he loaded loose cartridges into the chamber, a heavy thud landed on the tin roof.

All three pairs of eyes snapped toward the ceiling.

Thud. Thud.

A pair of heavy, cylindrical objects rolled down the corrugated slope.

The realization hit them in the exact same heartbeat.

"Out!"

They dove through the doorway just as the charges detonated.

The concussive shockwave ripped the wooden structure apart in an eruption of splintered timber, fire, and smoke.

Hurled through the air by the blast, Jakyeong slammed hard against the rocky earth, tumbling through the undergrowth.

He fought to clear the darkness from his eyes. High-pitched static screeched in his ears, his equilibrium entirely shattered. Pushing his palms against the dirt, he saw Han and Ryun sprawled several yards away, dazed and struggling to move.

Through the drifting haze of smoke and pulverized pine, a figure emerged down the path, cradling a suppressed tactical rifle.

Even on a deserted island in the middle of nowhere, the man was clad in a bespoke three-piece suit, his dark hair immaculately styled.

Kang Il-hyun.

Jakyeong ground his teeth, forcing his bruised knuckles into a fist to push himself up.

Before he could gain his footing, the heavy composite stock of the rifle swung through the smoke.

The blunt impact struck the side of his temple with concussive force, pitching his world into sudden, absolute blackness.
